working_theory_before: A two-gate subject-readiness model: subject-relative representation can improve discrimination, but conformal safety must be checked independently.
working_theory_after: Subject-relative normalization is a context-sensitive representation intervention, not a generally established repair. On the independent cohort it modestly improved discrimination and reduced ambiguous prediction sets, but the effect was smaller than preregistered and mean coverage fell below the safety floor. Representation gains therefore cannot be promoted to a reliable J-jump unless they survive an independent calibration-safety gate.

claim_updates.claim: Per-subject robust normalization produces a large, externally replicable accuracy repair.
claim_updates.reason: The accuracy change was +0.0436, below the frozen +0.08 threshold, and the paired-subject bootstrap interval included zero.

claim_updates.claim: Per-subject robust normalization can reduce conformal ambiguity on an independent wearable cohort.
claim_updates.reason: Full-set frequency fell by 0.0909 and the preregistered robustness loss fell by 0.0374.

claim_updates.claim: Representation improvement is sufficient evidence of a safe uncertainty repair.
claim_updates.reason: Accuracy and efficiency moved favorably while normalized mean coverage fell to 0.8681, below the frozen 0.88 floor.

claim_updates.claim: The direction of the representation effect is independent of protocol version.
claim_updates.reason: Accuracy improved in both V1 and V2, but the gains differed materially: +0.0147 versus +0.0742.

claim_updates.claim: The normalization effect is uniform across subjects.
claim_updates.reason: Only 63.64% of subjects had nonnegative accuracy change, with individual changes spanning -0.2917 to +0.2292.

meno_j_implication: The constructive leap is not the speculative transformation alone. The scientifically useful J-jump is a constrained proposal that passes independent effect-size, heterogeneity, and calibration-safety tests. Experiment 13 demonstrates why the falsification engine must be able to reject an appealing partial success.
next_falsification_target: Determine, with a newly frozen analysis, whether baseline reliability, protocol version, sensor quality, or distribution shift predicts who benefits from normalization without using post-outcome subgroup selection.
